comment: Keyword → page ownership registry. One keyword family = one page. Before writing any page, confirm every keyword you target is owned by THAT page. Volumes/KD: 2026-09 US, planner-exported; do not edit without new data.

bannedHeadTerms.reason: SERPs are TV hardware shopping (Samsung/LG/BestBuy), the A.I. movie on Netflix/Hulu, 'TV shows about AI' lists on IMDb/Wikipedia, job listings (Indeed/LinkedIn/ZipRecruiter), or the Left 4 Dead character. None of these visitors convert.
bannedHeadTerms.rule: Never optimize a title, H1, meta, or section around these bare terms. Long-tail phrases explicitly registered below (e.g. 'ai tv channel', 'ai tv show generator', 'how to launch an AI channel') are owned and allowed. A brand's verbatim tagline is allowed on that brand's channel page only.

/.note: The three spellings are the same audience — one page, never split.

/director.note: Highest volume × lowest KD of the money pages. NEVER target bare 'ai director'.

/tv-show-generator.note: ai episode generator (110/mo) is the biggest sub-term — give it its own H3.

/real-time.role: Explainer only, not a money page
/real-time.note: Low volume + mid KD. Exists to explain the concept and to justify the 'Realtime / Low-latency' filter tag. Never a homepage/category primary.

/interactive.note: Volume TBD. Positioned to catch the interactive-AI-video wave as it grows.

/channels.note: Tiny volume, near-zero competition — own both spellings early.

/creators.primary: how to launch an AI channel
secondary: how to start an AI livestream
/creators.note: Long-tail intent phrase; contains 'AI channel' but as registered long-tail, not the banned head term.

/channel/[slug].note: One page per verified channel in data/channels.json. Brand + ai livestream variant.
